pujas.title: Maha Mrityunjaya Jaap & Rudrabhishek
pujas.subtitle: For good health, long life & protection

about.q: What is the Maha Mrityunjaya Mantra?
about.a: Found in the Rig Veda and Yajur Veda, the Maha Mrityunjaya Mantra is a prayer to Lord Shiva as Tryambaka, the three-eyed one. It is chanted for healing, protection from untimely death and inner strength.
Mahakaleshwar in Ujjain is the Jyotirlinga of Shiva as Mahakal — the lord who is beyond time and death. Chanting this mantra in his presence is considered especially powerful.
Somvar is dedicated to Lord Shiva. A Rudrabhishek with milk, honey, curd, ghee and Ganga jal on this day is believed to please Mahadev quickly.

about.q: How do I take sankalp from home?
about.a: On the day of the puja, light a diya at home, sit facing east and chant 'Om Namah Shivaya' 108 times while the pandit performs the sankalp in your name.

temples.name: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham
temples.short: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on the western bank of the holy Ganga.
history: Kashi is believed to be the oldest living city in the world and the eternal abode of Lord Shiva.
Devotees believe that a darshan here and a dip in the Ganga bring liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
The newly built Kashi Vishwanath Corridor connects the temple directly with the ghats of the Ganga.

temples.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
temples.short: The nava-ratna temple of Maa Bhavatarini on the banks of the Hooghly.
history: Founded by Rani Rashmoni in 1855, the temple is dedicated to Maa Bhavatarini, a form of Kali.
Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa served here as a priest and attained his spiritual realisations in these precincts.
The complex includes twelve Shiva temples along the river and a Radha-Krishna temple.

temples.name: Maa Kamakhya Devalaya
temples.short: One of the most revered Shakti Peethas, atop the Nilachal hill.
history: Kamakhya is counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas and is a principal seat of Tantric worship.
The temple's beehive-shaped shikhara is a signature of the Nilachal style of architecture.
The annual Ambubachi Mela draws lakhs of devotees from across India.

temples.name: Maa Tara Temple, Tarapith
temples.short: The sacred Shakti Peetha of Maa Tara near the Dwaraka river.
history: Tarapith is revered as the place where the third eye of Devi Sati is believed to have fallen.
The great saint Bamakhepa worshipped Maa Tara here and his ashram still stands nearby.
Devotees come seeking protection, strength and freedom from fear.

temples.name: Shri Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.short: The south-facing Jyotirlinga, famed for the pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti.
history: Mahakaleshwar is the only Jyotirlinga that faces south (Dakshinamukhi), associated with Shiva as the lord of time.
The Bhasma Aarti performed before dawn is one of the most sacred rituals in Shaivism.
Ujjain hosts the Simhastha Kumbh on the banks of the Shipra every twelve years.

temples.name: Shri Jagannath Temple
temples.short: One of the Char Dham, home of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra.
history: The 12th-century temple is a masterpiece of Kalinga architecture.
The Mahaprasad cooked in the temple kitchen is offered to the deities and then shared among devotees.
The annual Rath Yatra is among the grandest festivals of India.

temples.name: Shri Somnath Jyotirlinga
temples.short: The first among the twelve Jyotirlingas, on the shore of the Arabian Sea.
history: Somnath is revered as the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva.
The temple has been rebuilt several times through history and stands as a symbol of faith and resilience.
The evening aarti with the sea in the background is a deeply moving experience.

site.name: Rudra Jyoti
site.description: Book pujas at sacred temples of India in your name and gotra, receive the puja video on WhatsApp and get the Aashirwad Box at your doorstep. Shop authentic puja samagri and spiritual products.

globalFaqs.q: Why should I book my puja with Rudra Jyoti?
globalFaqs.a: We work directly with temple pandits at each venue. Your name and gotra are recited in the sankalp, you receive a video of your puja, and we refund 100% if a puja cannot be performed for any reason.

globalFaqs.q: I don't know my gotra. What should I do?
globalFaqs.a: According to the shastras, when the gotra is not known the devotee may take sankalp with Kashyap gotra, as Rishi Kashyap is regarded as the progenitor of all. Simply tick “I don't know my gotra” while booking.
Experienced pandits associated with the temple perform every puja following the traditional vidhi of that temple.

globalFaqs.q: How will I know the puja was done in my name?
globalFaqs.a: Your name and gotra are read out during the sankalp. We share the puja video on your WhatsApp number, usually within 2–4 days of the puja.

globalFaqs.q: What will I receive after the puja?
globalFaqs.a: A video of the puja on WhatsApp within 2–4 days and, if you opted in, an Aashirwad Box with prasad and blessed items delivered within 8–10 days.

globalFaqs.q: Can I book for my family or someone living abroad?
globalFaqs.a: Yes. Choose a Couple, Family or Joint Family package and add their names. Devotees living outside India can book too — the video is shared on WhatsApp.

globalFaqs.q: What happens if the puja is not performed?
globalFaqs.a: If a puja is cancelled for any reason, you receive a 100% refund to the original payment method automatically.
Chat with us on WhatsApp or call our seva helpline between 8 AM and 9 PM IST, every day.
